FARRA:v2p175/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p175/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p175/r8.claim: لذكرا may be read with alif as a verbal noun; alternatively the alif represents possessive yāʾ for rhyme, or a vocative lament yāʾ.

NAHHAS:v3p33/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r13.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p33/r13.claim: Abu Ishaq offers two readings of لذكري: pray because prayer includes remembrance, or pray whenever you remember it.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r13.anchor: فيه قولان يكون المعنى أقم الصلاة لأن تذكرني فيها لأن الصلاة لا تكون إلا بذكر

NAHHAS:v3p33/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p33/r14.claim: Al-Nahhas adds a third: establish prayer so God will praise or mention you.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r14.anchor: وفيها قول ثالث يكون المعنى أقم الصلاة لأن أذكرك بالمدح

NAHHAS:v3p33/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن وأبو رجاء والشعبي
NAHHAS:v3p33/r15.claim: They read لذكرى; its final alif may be feminine or a substitute for yāʾ, chosen to align the verse endings.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r15.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن وأبو رجاء والشعبي ( أقم الصلاة لذكرى ) وفي هذه القراءة وجهان

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.claim: On the preceding question about divine istiwāʾ, the author says the sounder view of Abū ʿAlī is that it means power; the Kullābī account of an act or attribute called istiwāʾ is unintelligible.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.anchor: وإن كان الأصح ما ذهب إليه أبو علي أن المراد به الاقتدار

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r1.claim: References to God forgetting people mean abandoning them, never literal forgetfulness; nasiya an āyah means leaving it, and remembrance can mean knowledge rather than recollection.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r1.anchor: لأن الله تعالى لا ينسى وإنما معناه تركهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r2.claim: The divine remembrance in the report about remembering God means that God knows; likewise remembering a prayer means knowing it is due.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r2.anchor: فكذلك يكون معنى قوله: «إذا ذكرها» أي علمها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r3.claim: An overdue human debt is not canceled when its due time arrives unless the creditor releases it; God's obligations are even less likely to lapse without His permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r3.anchor: وهي مما يسقطها الإبراء كان في ديون الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r4.claim: By analogy with the agreed requirement to make up an intentionally missed Ramadan day, an intentionally missed prayer must also be made up.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r4.anchor: لو ترك يوما من رمضان متعمدا بغير عذر لوجب قضاؤه فكذلك الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r5.claim: Malik is reported to say that one who deliberately abandons prayer never makes it up; al-Qurtubi reads this as either saying the past cannot return or as severe warning, like reports on deliberate fasting.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r5.anchor: من ترك الصلاة متعمدا لا يقضي أبدا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r6.claim: Even on the severe-warning reading, the person must make up the prayer in place of its performance and repent; God then decides the outcome.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r6.anchor: ومع هذا فلا بد من توفية التكليف حقه بإقامة القضاء مقام الأداء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r7.speaker: أبو المطوس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r7.claim: Abū al-Muṭawwis reports from his father, from Abū Hurayra, a report that a deliberately missed Ramadan fast is not compensated even by lifelong fasting; al-Qurtubi calls the Abu Dawud report weak and, if sound, severe warning.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r7.anchor: وهذا يحتمل أن لو صح كان معناه التغليظ وهو حديث ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r8.claim: Sound reports establish expiation and include making up the missed day.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r8.anchor: وقد جاءت الكفارة بأحاديث صحاح، وفي بعضها قضاء اليوم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r9.claim: The instruction to make up a prayer after sleep or forgetfulness specifies that the sleeper is exempt from sin, not from the obligation, unlike a child before puberty.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#3/r9.anchor: والمراد بالرفع هنا رفع المأثم لا رفع الفرض عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r1.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that someone who remembers a missed prayer during an obligatory prayer should finish the current one and then pray the missed one; its transmitter ʿUmar ibn Abī ʿUmar is unknown.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r1.anchor: إذا ذكر أحدكم صلاة وهو في صلاة مكتوبة فليبدأ بالتي هو فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r2.claim: If authentic, the Ibn Abbas report supports al-Shāfiʿī's preference to begin with the current prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r2.anchor: وهذا لو صح كان حجة للشافعي في البداءة بصلاة الوقت

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the sound report of Jābir: at the Trench, the Prophet prayed the missed ʿAṣr after sunset and then prayed Maghrib, explicitly beginning with the missed prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r3.anchor: فصلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العصر بعد ما غربت الشمس، ثم صلى بعدها المغرب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r4.claim: The Trench report is especially clear because Maghrib has a single narrow time according to the Malikis and al-Shāfiʿī.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r4.anchor: ولا سيما والمغرب وقتها واحد مضيق غير ممتد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r5.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from Abū ʿUbayda, from his father, that at the Trench the Prophet made up four prayers in sequence: noon, afternoon, sunset, then night.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#4/r5.anchor: ثم أقام فصلى الظهر، ثم أقام فصلى العصر، ثم أقام فصلى المغرب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r1.claim: Scholars cite these reports for making up multiple missed prayers in the order they were missed when remembered together.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r1.anchor: وبهذا استدل العلماء على أن من فاتته صلاة قضاها مرتبة كما فاتته

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r2.claim: When one missed prayer is remembered during the tight time of a current prayer, Malik, al-Layth, al-Zuhrī, and others begin with the missed prayer, even if the current prayer's time expires.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r2.anchor: يبدأ بالفائتة وإن خرج وقت الحاضرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r3.speaker: الحسن والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r3.claim: A second view, held by al-Ḥasan, al-Shāfiʿī, hadith jurists, al-Muḥāsibī, and Ibn Wahb, begins with the current prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r3.anchor: يبدأ بالحاضرة وبه قال الحسن والشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r4.speaker: أشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r4.claim: Ashhab's third view lets the worshipper choose which prayer to perform first.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r4.anchor: الثالث: يتخير فيقدم أيتهما شاء، وبه قال أشهب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r5.claim: The first view reasons from the larger number of missed prayers, since all agree that the current prayer comes first when many have accumulated.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r5.anchor: وجه الأول: كثرة الصلوات ولا خلاف أنه يبدأ بالحاضرة مع الكثرة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r6.claim: Malik counts five or fewer missed prayers as a small number; some say four or fewer based on Jābir's report, while six is agreed to be many.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r6.anchor: فعن مالك: الخمس فدون، وقد قيل: الأربع فدون

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r7.claim: Whether one orders the missed prayer while already praying, all agree that a follower completes prayer with the imam first.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r7.anchor: فكل من قال بوجوب الترتيب ومن لم يقل به يقول، يتمادى مع الإمام

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar says the follower should pray with the imam, then the missed prayer, and repeat the prayer performed with the imam; al-Qurtubi says raising it to the Prophet was an error.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r8.anchor: إذا نسي أحدكم صلاة فلم يذكرها إلا وهو مع الإمام

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأحمد بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r9.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and Aḥmad say to perform the remembered missed prayer and then repeat the prayer offered with the imam, unless more than five prayers separate them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r9.anchor: يصلي التي ذكر، ثم يصلي التي صلى مع الإمام

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r10.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r10.claim: Al-Khiraqī reports Aḥmad's view: finish the current prayer, make up the missed one, and repeat the current prayer if time allows; if its time would expire, do not repeat it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r10.anchor: فإن خشي خروج الوقت وهو فيها أعتقد ألا يعيدها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r11.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r11.claim: Malik's apparent view is that someone remembering after two rakʿahs ends after two; if he is imam, his prayer and the congregation's prayer are invalidated.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r11.anchor: سلم من ركعتين، فإن كان إماما انهدمت عليه وعلى من خلفه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r12.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects that apparent invalidation as inconsistent with Malik's instruction to add a rakʿah after remembering following one, or a fourth after three, then end with a voluntary prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#5/r12.anchor: ولو انهدمت عليه كما ذكر وبطلت لم يؤمر أن يضيف إليها أخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r1.speaker: أبو قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r1.claim: Muslim's report from Abū Qatāda says sleep itself is not negligence; negligence is delaying prayer until the next prayer time, and a sleeper should pray on waking and pray the next day at its proper time.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r1.anchor: أما إنه ليس في النوم تفريط إنما التفريط على من لم يصل الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r2.speaker: عمران بن حصين
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r2.claim: A report from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn adds that whoever catches the next morning prayer should make up the missed one alongside it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r2.anchor: فمن أدرك منكم صلاة الغداة من غد صالحا فليقض معها مثلها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r3.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r3.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī knows no scholar who requires the repeated makeup; he suggests the instruction may be recommended to preserve the virtue of prayer at its time.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r3.anchor: وقال الخطابي: لا أعلم أحدا قال بهذا وجوبا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r4.speaker: عمران بن حصين
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r4.claim: In a sound report, the Prophet's party slept through sunrise, then prayed two rakʿahs and the dawn prayer after traveling; when asked about repeating them the next day, he replied that God accepts repayment from them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r4.anchor: أينهاكم الله عن الربا ويقبله منكم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects repeating a missed prayer beyond one makeup, relying on the Prophet's reply and the sound versions of ʿImrān's report, which omit the extra instruction; Abū Qatāda's wording is ambiguous.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r5.anchor: والصحيح ترك العمل لقوله عليه السلام: " أينهاكم الله عن الربا ويقبله منكم "

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r6.claim: The Prophet states that one who forgets a prayer should pray it when remembered, with no expiation beyond that; al-Ṭabarī notes some early authorities differed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#6/r6.anchor: من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك

TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين وأبو جعفر
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports that establishing prayer for God's remembrance means praying whenever one recalls an owed prayer, whether or not it is its appointed time; this is also attributed to al-Baqir.
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r2.anchor: قيل معناه أقم الصلاة متى ذكرت أن عليك صلاة كنت في وقتها أم لم تكن

TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r3.speaker: أنس
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r3.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that whoever forgets a prayer should perform it upon remembering, with no expiation other than that; Muslim records the report and other Sunni and Shiʿi routes transmit it.
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r3.anchor: من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها لا كفارة لها غير ذلك

THALABI:v6p239#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p239#2/r10.claim: Mujahid says establish prayer so that you remember God within it.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد: أقم الصلاة لتذكرني فيها

THALABI:v6p239#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r11.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p239#2/r11.claim: Maqatil says that if one misses prayer, one should perform it when one remembers it.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r11.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إذا تركت الصلاة ثم ذكرتها فأقمها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r5.claim: Moses is commanded to establish prayer in order to remember God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r11.claim: The author renders the prayer command as “perform prayer to remember Me,” while another reading means “pray when you remember.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r11.anchor: “Beni hatırında tutmak için namazı kıl” şeklinde tercüme ettiğimiz kısmına “Hatırladığında namazı kıl” mânası da verilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r12.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r12.claim: The Prophet said that whoever forgets a prayer should pray it when remembering, and then recited this verse, supporting the alternative rendering.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r12.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in “Bir namazı unutan kimse hatırladığında onu kılsın” buyurduktan sonra bu âyeti okuduğu rivayetiyle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r13.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r13.claim: Tabari considers the first rendering stronger in light of the verse’s wording.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r13.anchor: Taberî âyetin lafzına göre ilk mânanın daha kuvvetli olduğunu belirtir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r4.claim: The first instruction to Moses is also given to all messengers, and it presents three foundational duties.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r4.anchor: This is the first instruction given to Moses (sws) and it is something which has been given to all messengers of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r5.claim: Monotheism is religion’s central belief; messengers are first instructed to oppose the persistent human practice of associating partners with God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r5.anchor: the belief of monotheism is alluded to because it occupies the central place in religion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r6.claim: Every messenger was first directed to monotheism and launched an offensive against polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r6.anchor: an offensive against polytheism the foremost.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r7.claim: Worship belongs to God alone and entails obeying Him rather than willingly obeying anyone against His directives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r7.anchor: One of the consequences of this worship, as has been explained at other instances, is that He be obeyed too.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r8.claim: Worship means servitude, renewing obedience and sincerity, and remembering God; granting another the right to set religious law is polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r8.anchor: right for someone else. This is polytheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r9.claim: Prayer is to be performed diligently and is the greatest means of preserving remembrance of God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r9.anchor: It means to diligently offer it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r10.claim: Prayer is the greatest means of protecting God’s remembrance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r10.anchor: means to pr otecting God’s remembrance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r11.claim: Whether offered individually or collectively, prayer is God’s highest and most effective manifestation of remembrance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r11.anchor: and also its highest and most effective manifestation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p19/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p19/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p19/r1.claim: Through prayer, individuals and communities remember their covenant of servitude to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p19/r1.anchor: Through the prayer, a person keeps in remembrance his covenant

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p19/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p19/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p19/r2.claim: Neglecting prayer amounts to neglecting the whole religion, a danger linked to 19:59.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p19/r2.anchor: This has been explained under verse 59 of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r7.claim: After monotheism, Moses was first directed to prayer and specially reminded of the Hereafter; this matches the history of the prophets.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r7.anchor: after monotheism, it is the prayer to which Moses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r8.claim: Islahi laments that the Jews abandoned prayer and became indifferent to the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r8.anchor: the misfortune of the Jews is lamentable

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r9.claim: The Jewish scriptures mention sacrifice, but temple prayer only once, in Deuteronomy chapter 26.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r10.speaker: their jurists
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r10.claim: Some Jewish jurists hold that Moses never commanded prayer and that later editors added the Torah reference.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p20/r10.anchor: Some of their jurists even think that Moses (sws) never bade them to offer the prayer

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r4.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r4.claim: Exegetes gloss faʿbudnī as affirming God’s unity, citing creation of jinn and humans to worship Him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r5.claim: He reads faʿbudnī broadly as all commanded worship, then singles out prayer as the best and most useful act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r5.anchor: والأولى أن يكون فاعبدني لفظ يتناول ما كلفه به من العبادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r6.claim: Li-dhikrī may mean God remembers Moses with praise, or Moses remembers God exclusively without ostentation or distraction; it can also mean prayer’s appointed times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن تضاف إلى المفعول أي لأن أذكرك بالمدح والثناء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says grammar would normally say “for remembering it”; other readings mean remembering prayer means remembering God or supply “My prayer.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وكان حق العبادة أن يقال لذكرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r2.claim: A Prophetic report says a missed prayer is performed upon remembering and has no other expiation, then cites this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث بعد قوله: «فليصلها إذا ذكرها» قوله «إذ لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r3.speaker: السلمي والنخعي وأبو رجاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r3.claim: They read lil-dhikrā with the article and feminine alif, interpreting it as a reminder to pray when God reminds a person after forgetfulness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p318/r3.anchor: وقرأ السلمي والنخعي وأبو رجاء: للذكرى بلام التعريف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r9.claim: Knowledge of God is the first obligation; the name Allah gathers the meanings of the divine names, and only God fully bears their perfection, so worship belongs to him alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r9.anchor: فذكر الاسم العلم لأن هذا مقامه إذ الأنسب للملطوف به

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r10.claim: Prayer is the highest rite and the religion's core because constant remembrance sustains mindfulness and wards off evil; it joins divine majesty and beauty.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r10.anchor: لأنها أعلى شرائعه لأنها حاملة على المراقبة

SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r1.claim: The verbal noun may be possessed by its subject: لذكري can mean because I mentioned it in the scriptures or because I remember you.
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون المصدر مضافا لفاعله أي: لأني ذكرتها في الكتب، أو لأني أذكرك

SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r2.claim: The verbal noun may instead be possessed by its object, meaning that you remember Me.
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مضافا لمفعوله أي: لأن تذكرني

SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r3.claim: A reported explanation takes it as remembering prayer after forgetting it, supported by the Prophet's instruction to pray when one remembers a missed prayer.
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه ذكر الصلاة بعد نسيانها كقوله عليه السلام: " من نام عن صلاة أو نسيها فليصلها إذا ذكرها "

SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the expected wording would be لذكرها; proposed defenses are that remembering prayer means remembering God, that “my prayer” is elided, or that remembrance and forgetting ultimately come from God.
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وكان حق العبارة: " لذكرها ". ثم قال: " ومن يتمحل له أن يقول: إذا ذكر الصلاة فقد ذكر

SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء، السلمي
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r5.claim: Abu Raja and al-Sulami read للذكرى with the article and feminine alif; other forms are indefinite لذكرى and definite masculine للذكر.
SAMIN-DURR:20:14-15/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء والسلمي " للذكرى " بلام التعريف وألف التأنيث

ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r1.claim: One sense is to establish prayer in order to remember God, since prayer necessarily includes remembrance of Him.
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r1.anchor: أحدهما أقم الصلاة لأن تذكرني لأن الصلاة لا تكون إلا بذكر الله،

ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r2.speaker: الناس
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r2.claim: The other, customary sense is to pray whenever one remembers an owed prayer, even outside its time; forgetfulness is excused unless deliberately distracted, and a remembered prayer is performed even at sunrise or sunset.
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r2.anchor: والمعنى الثاني هو الذي عليه الناس ومعناه أقم الصلاة متى ذكرت أن عليك صلاة كنت في وقتها أو لم تكن،

ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r3.claim: A variant للذكرى means in the time of your remembrance.
ZAJJAJ:v3p352/r3.anchor: وقرئت للذكرى - معناه في وقت ذكرك.

ASAD-NOTES:20:14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:14/r1.claim: God declares that He alone is God and commands worship of Him alone; prayer's purpose is remembrance of Him.
ASAD-NOTES:20:14/r1.anchor: Verily, I - I alone - am God; there is no de ity save Me. Hence, worship Me alone

ASAD-NOTES:20:14#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:14#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:14#n10/r1.claim: Conscious remembrance of God's oneness and uniqueness is both the innermost purpose and the intellectual justification of all true prayer.
ASAD-NOTES:20:14#n10/r1.anchor: conscious remembrance of God and of His oneness and uniqueness is declared to be the innermost purpose, as well as the intellectual justification of all true prayer

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1080/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1080/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1080/r1.claim: God uses the singular in a context of affirming oneness and the plural in a context of majesty; Taha’s declaration “I am Allah” and the singular address in Maryam illustrate this.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1080/r1.anchor: إذا كان في مقام التوحيد يُفرِد وإذا كان في مقام التعظيم يجمع

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

QIRAAT-ER:20:14:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:14:1#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:20:14:1#1/r1.claim: This variant gives the final yāʾ of the first-person suffix a fatḥa, clarifying its pronunciation without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:20:14:1#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Variant adds explicit fatḥa on final yāʾ — phonetic clarification of the 1st person pronoun suffix

QIRAAT-ER:20:14:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:14:14#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:20:14:14#1/r1.claim: The variant places fatḥa on the yāʾ of dhikrī; the source identifies this as phonetic, with no semantic shift.
QIRAAT-ER:20:14:14#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍ, mutawatir: Fatḥa added to yāʾ of dhikrī — phonetic variant, no semantic shift

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16/r1.claim: The Prophet says that whoever forgets a prayer should perform it when he remembers, citing God’s command to establish prayer for His remembrance.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p16/r1.anchor: عن الزهري عن ابن المسيب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها فإن الله يقول ﴿ وأقم الصلاة لذكري ﴾

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r1.claim: Alusi treats the declaration that God alone is divine as a substitute for what is revealed; selection of Moses is not for this alone, but it foregrounds the foundational matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r1.anchor: اننى انا الله لا اله إلا انا ( بدل من ( ما يوحى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r7.claim: The fa orders worship after the declaration of exclusive divinity, since God's unique godhood entails worship being exclusively His.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r7.anchor: لترتيب المؤمور به على ما قبلها فان اختصاص الالوهيه به تعالى شأنه من موجبات تخصيص العباده به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r8.claim: Alusi prefers understanding worship here as ultimate submission and obedience to everything God commands.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r8.anchor: والمراد بها غاية التذلل والانقياد له تعالى في جميع ما يكلفه به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes worship here as monotheism, as in the verse saying jinn and humans were created to worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r9.anchor: المراد بها هنا التوحيد كما في قوله سبحانه ( وما خلقة الجن والانس إلا ليعبدون )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r10.claim: Prayer is singled out despite being included in worship because of its excellence and its encompassing remembrance through heart and tongue.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r10.anchor: خصت الصلاة بالذكر وافردت بالأمر مع اندراجها في الأمر في العباده لفضلها وانافتها على سائر العبادات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r11.claim: God calls prayer iman in the verse stating that He would not let their faith be lost.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r11.anchor: ايمانا في قوله سبحانه ( وما كان الله ليضيع ايمانكم )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r12.claim: Scholars disagree about whether someone who abandons prayer out of laziness is an unbeliever; Alusi refers the detailed discussion elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r12.anchor: واختلف العلماء في كفر تاركها كسلا كما فصل في محله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r13.claim: The apparent construction attaches li-dhikri to aqim: establish prayer in order to remember God within it; this explanation is reported from Mujahid.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r13.anchor: الظاهر أنه متعلق باقم أي اقم الصلاة لتذكرنى فيها لاشتمالها على الاذكار وروى ذلك عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r14.claim: A related reading is to keep remembering God and not forget Him; unlike the first, it makes ongoing prayer the cause that sustains ongoing remembrance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r14.anchor: وقريب منه ما قيل أي لتكون لى ذاكرا غير ناس فعل المخلصين في جعلهم ذكر ربهم على بال منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r15.claim: On the second reading, maintaining prayer helps sustain remembrance, as the command to seek help through patience and prayer also suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r15.anchor: لتستعين بها على استغراق فكرك وهمك فى الذكر كقوله تعالى ( واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r1.claim: Li-dhikri may attach to either worship or establishing prayer by shared governance; extending remembrance to inward and bodily acts also permits that construction, though it is less apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r1.anchor: وجوز أن يكون متعلقا باعبدنى أو باقم على أنه من باب الاعمال أي لتكون ذاكرا لى بالعبادة واقامة الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r2.claim: Some understand the phrase as requiring prayer purely for God, without showing off, mixing in remembrance of another, or pursuing another end.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r2.anchor: خاصة لا ترائى بها ولا تشوبها بذكر غيرى أو لاخلاص ذكرى وابتغاء وجهى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r3.claim: Another explanation makes prayer a means for God to remember the worshipper with praise and reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r3.anchor: أو لأن اذكرك بالثناء أي لاثنى عليك واثيبك بها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r4.claim: The phrase may refer to God's prior mention of prayer in the heavenly scriptures and His command to perform it.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r5.claim: Some take the lam temporally, meaning at the times of God's remembrance, namely the prayer times, as in the expression for five nights having passed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r5.anchor: أو لاوقات ذكرى وهى مواقيت الصلوات فاللام وقتيه بمعنى عند مثلها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r6.claim: Abu Ja'far reports the interpretation that prayer is to be made up when remembered; its lam may be temporal or causal, with several explanations for the omitted relation to prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r6.anchor: ومن الناس من حمل الذكر على ذكر الصلاة بعد نسيانها وروى ذلك عن أبى جعفر واللام حينئذ وقتيه أو تعليلية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r7.claim: In a sound report from Abu Hurayra, the Prophet slept through the dawn prayer, made it up, then cited this verse for the rule that a forgotten prayer is performed when recalled.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r7.anchor: حديث أبى هريرة أنه ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) نام عن صلاة الصبح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r8.claim: Alusi says the hadith does not require interpreting the verse as make-up prayer: recalling prayer recalls its purpose, remembrance of God, and thus motivates performing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r8.anchor: فان التعليل كما في الكشف صحيح والذكر على ما فسر في الوجه الأول واراد عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه إذا ذكر الصلاة انتقل من ذكرها إلى ذكر ما شرعت له

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r9.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r9.claim: Some verifiers say the verse implies that because God's remembrance is prayer's primary aim and is required always, one should promptly make up a missed appointed prayer; this is an implication, not its explicit wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171/r9.anchor: أنه لما جعل المقصود الاصلى من الصلاة ذكر الله تعالى وهو حاصل مطلوب في كل وقت فاذا فانه الوقت المحدود له ينبغى المبادرة اليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r1.claim: The possessive construction of dhikr with the pronoun can make the verbal noun's pronoun its object or its subject, depending on the interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r1.anchor: وإضافة ( ذكر ) إلى الضمير تحتمل أن تكون من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله وان تكون من اضافة المصدر إلى فاعله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r2.speaker: السلمي والنخعي وأبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r2.claim: Al-Sulami, al-Nakha'i, and Abu Raja read with the definite article and feminine alif: li-l-dhikra.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r2.anchor: النخعى وابو رجاء ( للذكرى ) بلام التعريف والف التانيث

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r3.speaker: فرقة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r3.claim: Another group reads li-dhikra with the feminine alif but without the definite article.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r3.anchor: وقرأت فرقة ( لذكرى ) بالف التانيث بغير لام التعريف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p171#2/r4.claim: A further group reads the masculine definite form li-l-dhikr.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r12.claim: The command to worship comes first to honor servitude; prayer follows as a sign of servitude and an ascent to the holy presence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r12.anchor: قدم هذا الأمر للاشارة إلى عظم شرف العبودية وثنى بقوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r7.claim: The address maps knowledge of God to the beginning, worship and prayer to the middle and bodily and spiritual practice, and the coming Hour to knowledge of the return.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r7.anchor: واشار سبحانه إلى علم المبدأ بقوله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v5p561/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r1.claim: Mujahid says that when a servant prays, he remembers his Lord.
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وأقم الصلاة لذكري} قال: إذا صلى عبد ذكر ربه

DURR-FULL:v5p561/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r2.claim: Ibrahim says the command is to pray when one remembers.
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم في قوله: {وأقم الصلاة لذكري} قال: حين تذكر

DURR-FULL:v5p561/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r3.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r3.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet’s ruling that whoever sleeps through or forgets a prayer should pray it when he remembers.
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r3.anchor: عن أنس: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إذا رقد أحدكم عن الصلاة أو غفل عنها فليصلها إذا ذكرها

DURR-FULL:v5p561/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra recounts that on a night journey after Khaybar, Bilal fell asleep while keeping watch and the party awoke after sunrise; they moved, performed ablution, prayed, and the Prophet said a missed prayer is performed upon remembering. Ibn Shihab read the phrase as li-l-dhikrā.
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: لما قفل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من خيبر أسري ليلة

DURR-FULL:v5p561/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r5.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r5.claim: Asked about missing prayer until sunrise or sunset, the Prophet prescribes approaching God, making ablution well, praying, and seeking forgiveness as the sole expiation.
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r5.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن رجل غفل عن الصلاة حتى طلعت الشمس أو غربت ما كفارتها

DURR-FULL:v5p561/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r6.claim: When Samura ibn Yahya told Ibn Abbas that he had forgotten the night prayer until morning, Ibn Abbas told him to get up and pray, citing this verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r6.anchor: عن سمرة بن يحيى قال: نسيت صلاة العتمة حتى أصبحت فغدوت إلى ابن عباس فأخبرته فقال: قم فصلها

DURR-FULL:v5p561/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says a forgotten prayer is made up whenever it is remembered.
DURR-FULL:v5p561/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: إذا نسيت صلاة فاقضها متى ذكرت

DURR-FULL:v5p562/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r1.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r1.claim: Al-Sha‘bi and Ibrahim say one should perform a forgotten prayer when one remembers it.
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي وإبراهيم في قوله: {وأقم الصلاة لذكري} قالا: صلها إذا ذكرتها

DURR-FULL:v5p562/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r2.claim: Ibrahim says whoever sleeps through or forgets a prayer must pray it whenever remembered, even at sunrise or sunset.
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: من نام عن صلاة أو نسيها يصلي متى ذكرها عند طلوع الشمس وعند غروبها

DURR-FULL:v5p562/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r3.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud reports that after the Prophet’s party slept through sunrise on the return from Hudaybiyya, the Prophet said to do as they normally did, as applies to anyone who sleeps or forgets.
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: أقبلنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الحديبية

DURR-FULL:v5p562/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r4.speaker: أبو جحيفة
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r4.claim: Abu Juhaifa reports that after the party slept until sunrise, the Prophet said God had returned their souls and whoever sleeps through or forgets a prayer should pray when awake or reminded.
DURR-FULL:v5p562/r4.anchor: عن أبي جحيفة قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفره الذي ناموا فيه حتى طلعت الشمس

BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r1.claim: The declaration is a substitute for what is revealed and demonstrates that knowledge of foundational creed precedes practical branches: divine oneness comes before worship.
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r1.anchor: وهو بدل من يوص دال على تقدم علم الأصول على الفروع فإن التوحيد من مسائل الأصول

BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r2.claim: Because God alone is deity, worship must be devoted to Him alone, without associating anyone with Him.
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r2.anchor: فإذا كان كذلك {فاعبدنى} فخصني بالعبادة والتوحيد

BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r3.claim: Prayer is singled out after the general command to worship because of its special merit.
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r3.anchor: {وأقم الصلواة} من عطف الخاص على العام لفضله

BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r4.claim: If remembrance is the object of the genitive, the prayer is performed so that the worshipper remembers God; proper remembrance engages tongue, heart, and limbs, all of which prayer gathers.
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r4.anchor: {لذكرى} من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله أي : لتذكرني

BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, remembrance may be a subject genitive: pray so that God remembers you through recompense.
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r5.anchor: أو من إضافته إلى فاعله أي لأذكرك بالإثابة

BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r6.claim: The verse inwardly calls for lasting intimate converse and presence with God, giving up the self to attain His continuous remembrance through theophany and annihilation of renewed existence.
BURSEVI:v5p285#2/r6.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : وأدم المناجات والمحاضرة معي ببذل الوجود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r13.claim: The following declaration and commands are the revelation Moses was ordered to hear; the sentence is an unrestricted apposition to “what is revealed.”

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r1.claim: God's proper name signifies the necessary existent, worthy of every praise; knowing the name God has made His own is the first divine matter Moses must know and the basis for the revealed rulings to follow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r1.anchor: ووقع الإخبار عن ضمير المتكلم باسمه العلم الدال على الذات الواجب الوجود المستحق لجميع المحامد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r2.claim: The naming also alludes to how people first introduce themselves by name: God knows His interlocutor Moses and makes His own name known to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r2.anchor: أن أول ما يتعارف به المتلاقون أن يعرفوا أسماءهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r3.claim: The Arabic name for God is Allāh; the Torah uses YHWH or Ehyeh in Exodus 3 and 6, though its frequent terms are “Lord” or “God,” perhaps reflecting translators' wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r3.anchor: ( يهوه ) أو ( أهيه ) المذكور في الإصحاح الثالث من سفر الخروج في التوراة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr notes further Torah occurrences of the name in Exodus 31:18 and 32:16, while suggesting that translators may account for the wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر اسم الله في مواضع من التوراة مثل الإصحاح الحادي والثلاثين من سفر الخروج في الفقرة الثامنة عشرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r5.claim: He observes that Ehyeh and YHWH have letters close to those of the Arabic word ilāh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r5.anchor: قريب الحروف من كلمة إله في العربية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r6.claim: He reports a view that the Hebrew divine name is “لاهم,” and suggests its final mīm may underlie the tanwīn in ilāh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r6.anchor: ولعل الميم في آخره هي أصل التنوين في إله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r7.claim: The emphatic particle reassures Moses, who is treated as potentially doubtful because the news is strange and might prompt doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r7.anchor: نزل منزلة الشاك لأن غرابة الخبر تعرض السامع للشك فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r8.claim: The separating pronoun adds emphasis, not exclusivity; the point is that the speaker bears the name Allāh, an identity predication rather than a derivational one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r8.anchor: لزيادة تقوية الخبر ، وليس بمفيد للقصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r9.claim: He compares the identity predication to the statement that the Messiah is God in 5:72.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r9.anchor: الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r10.claim: “There is no deity except Me” is a second predicate of inna's subject.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r11.claim: The declaration is intended to establish Moses' knowledge of God's oneness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r11.anchor: والمقصود منه حصول العلم لموسى بوحدانية الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r12.claim: The command to worship follows from God's sole divinity, which entails His exclusive right to worship; worship includes words and deeds of glorification and sincerity of heart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p199/r12.anchor: العبادة تجمع معنى العمل الدال على التعظيم من قول وفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r1.claim: Prayer is singled out because it gathers the states of worship; establishing it means maintaining it without neglect.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r2.claim: Dhikr may mean mental remembrance or verbal remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r2.anchor: بمعنى التذكر بالعقل ، ويجوز أن يكون الذكر باللسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r3.claim: The lām may express purpose: pray in order to remember God, since prayer recalls the Creator through the worshipper's sense of standing before Him in intimate conversation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r3.anchor: أي أقم الصلاة لأجل أن تذكرني ، لأن الصلاة تذكر العبد بخالقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r4.claim: Together with 29:45, the purpose of prayer implies piety: remembering God's commands and prohibitions leads the worshipper to obey and avoid what He forbids; Moses receives this wisdom generally, while Muhammad receives it in detail.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r4.anchor: يظهر أن التقوى من حكمة مشروعية الصلاة لأن المكلف إذا ذكر أمر الله ونهيه فعل ما أمره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r5.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks time: establish prayer at the time appointed for God's remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r5.anchor: للتوقيت ، أي أقم الصلاة عند الوقت الذي جعلته لذكري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r6.claim: On another reading, verbal remembrance moves the heart, includes praise and acknowledgment of God's right, and points to the wisdom in prayer times; the context supplies an ellipsis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p200/r6.anchor: لأن ذكر اللسان يحرك ذكر القلب ويشتمل على الثناء على الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p203/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p203/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p203/r4.claim: The address reasons through each command and prohibition: identify God and His oneness, derive worship and prayer, affirm the Hour and its requital, warn against deniers, and show that violating the warning brings ruin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p203/r4.anchor: فابتدىء بالإعلام بأن الذي يكلمه هو الله ، وأنه لا إله إلا هو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r1.claim: The command to worship means to worship God alone.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r2.claim: Most interpreters say to pray whenever one remembers an owed prayer, whether or not its prescribed time remains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما أقم الصلاة متى ذكرت أن عليك صلاة سواء كنت في وقتها أو لم تكن هذا قول الأكثرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r3.speaker: أنس عن النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r3.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said whoever forgets a prayer should perform it when he remembers, with no expiation other than that.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r3.anchor: وروى أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انه قال من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها لا كفارة لها غير ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says the prayer is performed so that the worshipper remembers God during it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r4.anchor: والثاني أقم الصلاة لتذكرني فيها قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud, Ubayy ibn Kab, and Ibn al-Sumayfa read li-l-dhikrā with two lām letters and a doubled dhāl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وابن السميفع وأقم الصلاة للذكرى بلامين وتشديد الذال

MUJAHID:v1p394#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p394#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p394#3/r1.claim: When a servant prays, he remembers his Lord.
MUJAHID:v1p394#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وأقم الصلاة لذكري ﴾ يقول إذا صلى عبد ذكر ربه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r1.claim: Worship God by affirming His oneness and obeying Him.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r2.claim: The phrase means to remember God in prayer because prayer contains invocations.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r2.anchor: لتذكرني فيها لاشتمال الصلاة على الأدكار

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r3.claim: Alternatively, the prayer is for God's remembrance because He mentioned and commanded it in the scriptures.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r3.anchor: أو لأني ذكرتها في الكتب وأمرت بها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r4.claim: Alternatively, prayer is so that God may remember the worshipper with praise.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r5.claim: Alternatively, it is for God's remembrance alone, without mixing in remembrance of anyone else.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r5.anchor: أو لذكري خاصة لا تشوبه بذكر غيري

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r6.claim: Alternatively, it means that the worshipper should remember God without forgetting Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r6.anchor: أو لتكون لي ذاكرا غير ناس

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r7.claim: Alternatively, it means at the times of God's remembrance, namely the prayer times, as in 4:103.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r7.anchor: أو لأوقات ذكري وهي مواقيت الصلاة لقوله إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r8.claim: It has also been interpreted as praying after forgetting; this requires ellipsis of the annexed noun, meaning remembrance of my prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r8.anchor: وقد حمل على ذكر الصلاة بعد نسيانها وذا يصح بتقدير حذف المضاف أي لذكر صلاتي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r9.claim: The verse shows that no obligatory act after monotheism is greater than prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#7/r9.anchor: وهذا دليل على أنه لا فريضة بعد التوحيد أعظم منها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r1.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it should pray it when remembering, citing the command to establish prayer for God’s remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r1.anchor: من نام عن صلاة أو نسيها فليصلها إذا ذكرها فإن الله عز وجل يقول: { وأقم الصلاة لذكري }

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r2.claim: Anas ibn Mālik reports that, when asked about someone asleep or heedless of prayer, the Prophet said its expiation is to pray it upon remembering; Ibrahim ibn Tahmān and Hammām ibn Yaḥyā corroborate Hajjāj’s report from Qatāda.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r3.claim: Al-Dāraquṭnī reports from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet said a forgotten prayer’s time is when it is remembered.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r3.anchor: وروى الدارقطني عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r4.claim: The report makes makeup obligatory for a sleeper or forgetful person, whether one prayer or many; this is the majority view, while an anomalous view excuses makeup beyond five prayers, contrary to the hadith.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r4.anchor: فقوله: «فليصلها إذا ذكرها» دليل على وجوب القضاء على النائم والغافل، كثرت الصلاة أو قلت، وهو مذهب عامة العلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r5.claim: God commands prayer at specified times; doing at night what was commanded for day, or vice versa, fails to fulfill the command and earns no reward, so makeup rests on a renewed Prophetic command rather than the original one.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r5.anchor: قلت: أمر الله تعالى بإقامة الصلاة، ونص على أوقات معينة، فقال: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس [الإسراء: 78] الآية وغيرها من الآي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r6.claim: Without the Prophet’s instruction to pray upon remembering, no one could benefit from a prayer offered outside its time; by this reasoning makeup is a new obligation, not performance under the original command.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r6.anchor: من نام عن صلاة أو نسيها فليصلها إذا ذكرها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r7.claim: The majority also requires an intentional prayer-abandoner to make it up despite sin; Dāwūd and the Shāfiʿī Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ashʿarī dissent, as Ibn al-Qaṣṣār reports.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r7.anchor: فأما من ترك الصلاة متعمدا، فالجمهور أيضا على وجوب القضاء عليه، وإن كان عاصيا إلا داود.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r8.claim: The difference is liability for sin: the deliberate abandoner sins, unlike the forgetful or sleeper, but all must make up the prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r8.anchor: والفرق بين المتعمد والناسي والنائم، حط المأثم فالمتعمد مأثوم وجميعهم قاضون.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r9.claim: The general command to establish prayer does not distinguish between praying on time and afterward, and an imperative entails obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r9.anchor: والحجة للجمهور قوله تعالى: { وأن أقيموا } ولم يفرق بين أن يكون في وقتها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r10.claim: Because sleepers and forgetful people, who are not sinful, are commanded to make up prayer, the deliberate abandoner is even more obligated to do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r10.anchor: وأيضا فقد ثبت الأمر بقضاء النائم والناسي، مع أنهما غير مأثومين، فالعامد أولى.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:14/r11.claim: The author notes that forgetfulness can mean leaving something, as the Qurʾān uses it; the excerpt ends before the cited verse.

QASHANI:20:14-15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:14-15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:14-15/r1.claim: The emphatic declaration and shift from Lord to God keep Moses from stopping at the divine attributes and names and becoming veiled from the Essence; the Lord is the disclosed name through which guidance comes.
QASHANI:20:14-15/r1.anchor: بالتأكيد، وتبديل الرب بالله لئلا يقف مع الصفات في الحضرة الأسمائية

QASHANI:20:14-15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:14-15/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:14-15/r2.claim: The one God is described by every attribute, yet divine unity and selfhood do not multiply through the many manifestations and attributes.
QASHANI:20:14-15/r2.anchor: لم أتكثر ولم يتعدد أنائيتي وأحديتي بكثرة المظاهر وتعدد الصفات

QASHANI:20:14-15/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:14-15/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:14-15/r3.claim: Worship is directed to the Essence rather than its names and attributes, preparing the annihilation of selfhood in the divine Reality and essential glorification.
QASHANI:20:14-15/r3.anchor: خصص عبادتك بذاتي دون أسمائي وصفاتي بالعبادة الذاتية وتهيئة استعداد فناء الأنية في حقيقتي

QASHANI:20:14-15/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:14-15/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:14-15/r4.claim: The commanded prayer is spiritual witnessing of the Essence, above the heart's presence that remembers the attributes.
QASHANI:20:14-15/r4.anchor: صلاة الشهود الروحي لذكر ذاتي فوق صلاة الحضور القلبي لذكر صفاتي

RAZI-FULL:v22p34/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p34/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p34/r1.claim: Moses had received six demanding charges: knowledge of oneness, worship and prayer, the Hereafter, wisdom in God's acts, great signs, and a mission to the most defiant people.
RAZI-FULL:v22p34/r1.anchor: أحدها : معرفة التوحيد : { إننى أنا الله لا إلاه إلا أنا }

STUDYQURAN:20:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r1.claim: Compare 3:18, where God likewise testifies that there is no god but He.
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r1.anchor: See also 3:18, where God testifies to His own Divinity

STUDYQURAN:20:14/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r2.claim: Performing prayer for God's remembrance refers to remembering God often during the prayer.
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r2.anchor: perform the prayer for the remembrance of Me is said to refer to the act of remembering God much in the prayer

STUDYQURAN:20:14/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r3.speaker: Rūzbihān al-Baqlī
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r3.claim: Rūzbihān al-Baqlī describes prayer as the servant becoming remembrance, immersed in witnessing the Remembered One, with disclosure of divine secrets and beauty to ascending spirits.
STUDYQURAN:20:14/r3.anchor: as explained by the Sufi Rūzbihān al-Baqlī, for the servant to be the dhikr through which he becomes “drowned in the oceans of witnessing the One Who is Remembered

TAB-FULL:v16p31/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r1.speaker: عامة قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says the doubled-nun and open-alif reading was read by the general readers of Kufa; it connects “I chose you” with the prior call to Moses.
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r1.anchor: وبهذه القراءة قرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفة

TAB-FULL:v16p31/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r2.speaker: عامة قراء المدينة والبصرة وبعض أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r2.claim: Most Medinan and Basran readers and some Kufans read the nūn light, as a statement by God that He chose Moses.
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r2.anchor: وأما عامة قراء المدينة والبصرة وبعض أهل الكوفة فقرءوه: {وأنا اخترتك} [طه: 13] بتخفيف النون على وجه الخبر من الله عن نفسه

TAB-FULL:v16p31/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r3.claim: Al-Tabari accepts both readings: Quran scholars recited each one, their meanings agree, and either reading is correct.
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي أن يقال: إنهما قراءتان قد قرأ بكل واحدة منهما قراء أهل العلم بالقرآن، مع اتفاق معنييهما

TAB-FULL:v16p31/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r4.claim: God chose Moses and elected him for His message to those to whom He would send him; Moses must listen to the revelation, retain it, and act on it.
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r4.anchor: وتأويل الكلام: نودي أنا اخترناك، فاجتبيناك لرسالتنا إلى من نرسلك إليه فاستمع إلى ما يوحى

TAB-FULL:v16p31/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r5.claim: God alone is the deity worthy of worship; no other being is fit to be worshipped, so worship must be devoted exclusively to Him.
TAB-FULL:v16p31/r5.anchor: إنني أنا المعبود الذي لا تصلح العبادة إلا له، لا إله إلا أنا فلا تعبد غيري

TAB-FULL:v16p32/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r1.claim: Mujahid says establishing prayer is for remembering God in it: when a person prays, he remembers his Lord.
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {أقم الصلاة لذكري} [طه: 14] قال: إذا صلى ذكر ربه

TAB-FULL:v16p32/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r2.claim: Ibrahim interprets the command as performing the prayer when one remembers it.
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r2.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {وأقم الصلاة لذكري} [طه: 14] قال: يصليها حين يذكرها

TAB-FULL:v16p32/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r3.claim: The Prophet says that whoever forgets a prayer should pray it when he remembers, citing God's command to establish prayer for His remembrance.
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها، قال الله: {أقم الصلاة لذكري} [طه: 14]

TAB-FULL:v16p32/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r4.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r4.claim: Al-Zuhri is reported to recite the phrase in a form he treats like “my action.”
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r4.anchor: وكان الزهري يقرؤها: {أقم الصلاة لذكري} [طه: 14] بمنزلة فعلي

TAB-FULL:v16p32/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers “establish prayer so that you remember Me in it,” the more apparent meaning; if the command meant “when you remember the prayer,” it would have said “for its remembrance.”
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r5.anchor: وأولى التأويلين في ذلك بالصواب تأويل من قال: معناه: أقم الصلاة لتذكرني فيها، لأن ذلك أظهر معنييه

TAB-FULL:v16p32/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r6.claim: If al-Zuhri's reading were widely transmitted among regional readers, it would support the alternative “pray when you remember it,” construing the form as “for its remembrance” with the suffix omitted to fit the verse endings.
TAB-FULL:v16p32/r6.anchor: وذلك أن الزهري وجه بقراءته {أقم الصلاة لذكري} [طه: 14] بالألف لا بالإضافة، إلى أقم لذكراها

TAB-FULL:v16p34/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p34/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p34/r1.claim: The cited poem says “to my mother” as “to ma”; Arabic also says “O father and mother” intending “O my father and my mother,” supporting omission or alteration of the suffix in the reading discussed.
TAB-FULL:v16p34/r1.anchor: أطوف ما أطوف ثم آوي … إلى أما ويرويني النقيع

SULAMI:v1p437#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti urges Moses to let no deed or word occupy his heart besides God, and to live in the beginningless and endless rather than in passing times and ages.
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : لا يشغل قلبك بغيري فعلا

SULAMI:v1p437#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says the verse points to God's reality: references to beginning, end, times, and epochs are limitations that do not apply to Him.
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : إشارة إلى حقيقة الحق

SULAMI:v1p437#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r3.claim: God commands worship to make the creatures recognize their need and helplessness, not because He needs their service or is self-sufficient through it.
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r3.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : أظهر هذا الخلق في شموخ

SULAMI:v1p437#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r4.claim: Al-Wasiti says God addressed Moses in Hebrew and described Himself to Muhammad in Arabic; the change of language does not change the divine attribute, just as commands and prohibitions vary without changing it.
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : بالعبرانية خاطب موسى ثم وصف لمحمد

SULAMI:v1p437#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r5.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r5.claim: Al-Husayn says the declaration removes every deity from human beings; once the inner secret is free of reverence for another, this declaration is no longer needed.
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r5.anchor: قال الحسين : ﴿ لا إله إلا أنا ﴾ تنظيف البشر

SULAMI:v1p437#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r6.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r6.claim: Al-Wasiti sees the verse's sequence as beginning with unity of God and ending with the language of obedience in the command to establish prayer for His remembrance.
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r6.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : ^ ( إنني إنا الله لا إله أنا فاعبدني ) ^ ابتدأه

SULAMI:v1p437#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r7.claim: Ibn Ata reads establishing prayer for God's remembrance as remaining with Him in proper adab and not becoming heedless while turning toward Him.
SULAMI:v1p437#3/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أقم معي بحسن الأدب

TABATABAI:20:14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:14/r1.claim: The command to worship follows God’s self-identification because all things begin from Him, subsist through Him, and return to Him; therefore He alone is the true deity worthy of worship.
TABATABAI:20:14/r1.anchor: إذا كان هو الذي منه يبدأ كل شيء وبه يقوم وإليه يرجع فلا ينبغي أن يخضع خضوع العبادة إلا له فهو الإله المعبود بالحق

TABATABAI:20:14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:14/r2.claim: Prayer is singled out after the general command to worship as the specific after the general, because it is the best expression of servitude and embodies remembrance of God.
TABATABAI:20:14/r2.anchor: لأن الصلاة أفضل عمل يمثل به الخضوع العبودي ويتحقق بها ذكر الله سبحانه تحقق الروح بقالبه

TABATABAI:20:14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:14/r3.claim: The verbal noun is annexed to its object, and the purposive lām attaches to establish: make your remembrance of God actual through prayer.
TABATABAI:20:14/r3.anchor: من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله واللام للتعليل وهو متعلق بأقم

TABATABAI:20:14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r4.claim: A reported alternative attaches لذكري to the preceding command فاعبدني rather than to أقِم.
TABATABAI:20:14/r4.anchor: وقيل بقوله { فاعبدني } ثم اللام قيل للتعليل

TABATABAI:20:14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r5.claim: One reported reading takes the lām as purposive; another takes it as temporal, meaning pray at My remembrance or when you remember a prayer you missed.
TABATABAI:20:14/r5.anchor: وقيل للتوقيت والمعنى أقم الصلاة عند ذكري أو عند ذكرها إذا نسيتها أو فاتت منك

TABATABAI:20:14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r6.claim: The temporal reading is compared with the lām in the command to establish prayer at the sun’s decline, 17:78.
TABATABAI:20:14/r6.anchor: فهي كاللام في قوله أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس

TABATABAI:20:14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r7.claim: One view understands dhikr as verbal remembrance recited within the prayer.
TABATABAI:20:14/r7.anchor: ثم الذكر قيل المراد به الذكر اللفظي الذي تشتمل عليه الصلاة

TABATABAI:20:14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r8.claim: Another view takes dhikr as inward remembrance that accompanies prayer, is realized by it, or results from it as an effect of its cause.
TABATABAI:20:14/r8.anchor: وقيل الذكر القلبي الذي يقارنها ويتحقق بها أو يترتب عليها ويحصل بها حصول المسبب عن سببه

TABATABAI:20:14/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r9.claim: Other views understand remembrance as what precedes prayer or as both inward and outward remembrance together.

TABATABAI:20:14/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r10.claim: An alternative treats the verbal noun as annexed to its subject: pray so God remembers the worshipper with praise and reward, or because He mentioned and commanded prayer in scripture.
TABATABAI:20:14/r10.anchor: وقيل من إضافة المصدر إلى فاعله والمراد صل لأن أذكرك بالثناء والإثابة أو المراد صل لذكري إياها في الكتب السماوية

TABATABAI:20:14/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r11.claim: One interpretation says the phrase restricts prayer to remembrance of God, excluding other aims such as seeking reward or fearing punishment; another denies that this restriction is implied.
TABATABAI:20:14/r11.anchor: وقيل إنه يفيد قصر الإقامة في الذكر، والمعنى أقم الصلاة لغرض ذكري لا لغرض آخر غير ذكري

TABATABAI:20:14/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r12.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r12.claim: Another proposed restriction is to pray for God’s remembrance alone, without showing off or mixing in remembrance of another; a counterview says the wording does not entail it.
TABATABAI:20:14/r12.anchor: وقيل إنه يفيد قصر المضاف في المضاف إليه، والمراد أقم الصلاة لذكري خاصة من غير أن ترائي بها

TABATABAI:20:14/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:14/r13.claim: Some take dhikr to mean remembering prayer itself: pray when recalling it or for its remembrance, with an omitted word for My prayer, or by naming the effect while intending its cause.
TABATABAI:20:14/r13.anchor: وقيل المراد بالذكر ذكر الصلاة أي أقم الصلاة عند تذكرها أو لأجل ذكرها والكلام على تقدير مضاف

TABATABAI:20:14/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:14/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:14/r14.claim: After surveying the various interpretations, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the initial, contextually immediate reading: establish prayer so that remembrance of God is realized through it.
TABATABAI:20:14/r14.anchor: والذي يسبق إلى الفهم هو ما قدمناه

THALABI:v6p240/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p240/r1.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v6p240/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction that anyone who forgets a prayer or sleeps through it should pray when remembering it, citing God's command to establish prayer for His remembrance.
THALABI:v6p240/r1.anchor: عن أنس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

THALABI:v6p240/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p240/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p240/r2.claim: Another reading of the connection takes “for My remembrance” as returning to the preceding command: listen to the revelation and listen to My remembrance.
THALABI:v6p240/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو مردود على الوحي يعني فاستمع لما يوحى واستمع لذكري

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#5/r1.claim: The prayer is established so that the worshipper remembers God within it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p277#5/r1.anchor: وأقم الصلاة لذكري} أي لتذكرني فيها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r1.speaker: العامة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r1.claim: The common interpretation is to perform an owed prayer whenever one remembers it, whether or not its appointed time remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما -وهو الذي عليه العامة-: أن معناه أقم الصلاة متى ذكرت أن عليك صلاة، كنت في وقتها أو لم تكن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r2.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says that whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it should pray when remembering it, citing this verse; no grading is given.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r2.anchor: وهذا المعنى ما روي أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: "من نسي صلاة، أو نام عنها فليصلها إذا ذكرها، إن الله عز وجل يقول:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan takes the command to mean praying in order to remember God, since prayer necessarily includes God’s remembrance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r3.anchor: والثاني: معناه أقم الصلاة لأن تذكرني؛ لأن الصلاة لا تكون إلا بذكر الله. وهذا قول الحسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says that when a servant prays, the servant remembers the Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r4.anchor: ومجاهد قال: (إذا صلى عبد ذكر ربه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371#2/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba chooses the sense “so that you remember Me in it.”

NAHHAS:v3p35/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p35/r9.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v3p35/r9.claim: Another analysis connects the purpose clause to the command establish prayer for My remembrance, so that each soul is repaid.
NAHHAS:v3p35/r9.anchor: وقيل المعنى أقم الصلاة لذكري لتجزى كل نفس بما تسعى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r1.claim: A rigid insistence on a hand behind every mention of the right hand can flatten the Shammākh phrase into the trivial statement that a grasp uses the right hand.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r1.anchor: فإن اعتبار الأصل الذي قدمت وهو أنك لا ترى اليمين حيث لا معنى لليد يقف بنا على الظاهر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r2.claim: Al-Khansāʾ’s image of extending a hand toward glory means much the same as receiving glory’s banner in the right hand, showing how figurative use remains connected to its source.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r2.anchor: لم تجد فرقا بين أن يمد إلى المجد يدا وبين أن يتلقى رايته باليمين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r3.claim: Treating figurative names as severed from their original sense leads to grave misreadings and strained interpretations of distinguished speech.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r3.anchor: هذا الضرب من الغلط كالداء الدوي حقه أن يستقصي في الكي عليه والعلاج منه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r4.claim: In 50:37, Jurjānī says a person who fails to understand is pictured as though deprived of a heart, rather than simply using heart as a synonym for intellect; he compares this to figurative loss of sight or hearing.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p312/r4.anchor: أخذه ساذجا وقلبه غفلا وقال القلب ههنا بمعنى العقل

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r6.speaker: author
