TABATABAI:20:11-14/r6.claim: The first divine address clears the setting of others for revelation; the later 'I am Allah' is the revealed message itself, so it is not redundant.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r6.anchor: لأن الأول تخلية للمقام من الأغيار

TABATABAI:20:13-14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r5.claim: The following eleven verses include prophecy and mission: prophecy is stated first, while the mission begins with Moses' staff question and ends with the order to go to Pharaoh; Moses is called both prophet and messenger elsewhere.
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r5.anchor: هذا هو الوحي الذي أمر عليه السلام بالاستماع له في إحدى عشرة آية تشتمل على النبوة والرسالة معا

TABATABAI:20:13-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r6.claim: These verses state monotheism and resurrection while leaving prophecy implicit because God addresses a prophet; practical religion is condensed into worship, completing belief and practice.
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r6.anchor: وأصول الاعتقاد ثلاثة التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد وقد ذكر منها التوحيد والمعاد وطوي عن النبوة

TABATABAI:20:13-14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r7.claim: God identifies the present speaker with the name Allah rather than describing God as the speaker; the divine essence is inaccessible, but the named, present one can answer 'I am that one,' as Joseph did.

TABRISI:20:12-14/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:12-14/r15.claim: Only God deserves worship; He commands Moses to worship Him alone, without associating anyone, and to convey this to his people.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r15.anchor: أي لا إله يستحق العبادة غيري

TABRISI:20:12-14/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r16.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
TABRISI:20:12-14/r16.claim: Hasan and Mujahid understand this as praying so that one remembers God through glorifying and magnifying Him.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r16.anchor: لأن الصلاة لا تكون إلا بذكر الله عن الحسن ومجاهد

TABRISI:20:12-14/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:12-14/r17.claim: Another explanation is that God will remember Moses with praise and commendation.

TABRISI:20:12-14/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r18.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:20:12-14/r18.claim: Abu Muslim reads it as a command to pray to God alone, rather than praying as idolaters do.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r18.anchor: صل لي ولا تصل لغيري كما يفعله المشركون عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:20:12-14/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r19.speaker: أكثر المفسرين وأبو جعفر
TABRISI:20:12-14/r19.claim: Most commentators, and a report from Abu Ja'far, take it as a command to perform a prayer whenever one remembers it, whether or not its appointed time has arrived.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r19.anchor: أقم الصلاة متى ذكرت أن عليك صلاة كنت في وقتها أم لم تكن

TABRISI:20:12-14/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r20.speaker: أنس
TABRISI:20:12-14/r20.claim: The commentary says this final interpretation is supported by a report from Anas back to the Prophet, but the excerpt gives no report text.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r20.anchor: ويعضده ما رواه أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r8.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction that whoever forgets a prayer must pray it on remembering; prayer is its only expiation, as Qatāda connects to this verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r8.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r9.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it should pray upon remembering; Qatāda cites this verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r9.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من نسي صلاة أو نام عنها فليصلها إذا ذكرها» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r10.claim: A report through Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib attributes the same instruction about forgotten or sleep-missed prayer to the Prophet.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r10.anchor: عن الزهري، عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من نسي الصلاة أو نام عنها فليصلها إذا ذكرها» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r11.speaker: ابن مجاهد عن أبيه
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r11.claim: Ibn Mujāhid, transmitting from his father, says the servant remembers God when he prays.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r11.anchor: وتفسير ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: إذا صلى العبد ذكر الله.

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r6.claim: God is transcendent from defect and likeness by His entitlement to majesty and beauty.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r6.anchor: تقدست عن الأعلال في أزلي ، وتنزهت ( . . . ) والأشكال باستحقاقي لجلالي وجمالي

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r7.claim: In the Real's existence, all others are absent; forms and traces vanish when His reality is established.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r7.anchor: والرسوم والأطلال عند ثبوت حقي محو

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r8.claim: Worship means submitting to God's decree, carrying out His command, and yielding to the might of His dominion.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r8.anchor: أي تذلل لحكمي ، وأنفذ أمري ، واخضع لجبروت سلطاني

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r9.claim: Prayer performed without awareness of its true Originator produces self-admiration.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r9.anchor: إقامتها من غير ملاحظة مجريها ومنشيها يورث الإعجاب

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r10.claim: When a servant prays in witness and realizes another than himself establishes the prayer, it opens communion and the station of intimate nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r10.anchor: وإذا أقام العبد صلاته على نعت الشهود والتحقق بأن مجريها غيره كانت الصلاة بهذا فتحا لباب المواصلة . والوقوف على محل النجوى

BURHAN:v4p29/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p29/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p29/r4.claim: An impersonal pronoun whose antecedent is neither stated nor contextually known requires explanation by a word or clause; these include the pronoun of affair.
BURHAN:v4p29/r4.anchor: السادس إلا يعود على مذكور ولامعلوم بالسياق أو غيره وهو الضمير المجهول

BURHAN:v4p29/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p29/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p29/r5.claim: The singular pronoun in نعم and بئس is explained by a word, while a clause explains the pronoun of affair or story.
BURHAN:v4p29/r5.anchor: فالمفرد في نعم وبئس والجملة ضمير الشأن والقصة

BURHAN:v2p410/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p410/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p410/r1.claim: The explicit pronoun can serve solely to magnify the speaker.
BURHAN:v2p410/r1.anchor: وقد يكون لمجرد التعظيم كقوله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p103/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p103/r1.speaker: ابن خروف والصفار وابن عمرو
BURHAN:v4p103/r1.claim: These grammarians allow conjunction across sentence moods: an imperative with a report, and a prohibition with an imperative or report.
BURHAN:v4p103/r1.anchor: وخالفهم كثير من النحويين كابن خروف والصفار وابن عمرو وقالو يعطف الامر على الخبر والنهي على الامر والخبر

BURHAN:v3p435/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p435/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p435/r6.claim: أقم الصلاة means complete the prayer as commanded.
BURHAN:v3p435/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ أقم الصلاة ﴾ 3 أي أتمها كما أمرت

NASHR:v2p322/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r5.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p322/r5.claim: For five yāʾs of annexation—إني آنست, إني أنا ربك, إنني أنا الله, لنفسي اذهب, and في ذكري—the two Medinese, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read the yāʾ open.
NASHR:v2p322/r5.anchor: إني آنست، إني أنا ربك، إنني أنا الله، لنفسي اذهب، في ذكري اذهبا

NASHR:v2p322/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r8.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p322/r8.claim: The two Medinese and Abu Amr open the yāʾ in لذكري إن, ويسر لي أمري, على عيني, إذ تمشي برأسي, and إني.
NASHR:v2p322/r8.anchor: على عيني إذ تمشي برأسي إني فتح الأربعة

NASHR:v2p322/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p322/r10.claim: By Abu Ja'far's general rule, the yāʾs should be open where he cuts the hamza, but Ibn al-Jazari found no explicit transmission for that inference.
NASHR:v2p322/r10.anchor: مذهب أبي جعفر فتحها لمن قطع الهمزة عنه، ولكني لم أجده منصوصا

NASHR:v2p143/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p143/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p143/r1.claim: Readers agree to omit the final alif of أنا in connected recitation and retain it at pause; when followed by hamzat qaṭʿ, its omission in connection is disputed.
NASHR:v2p143/r1.anchor: أجمعوا على حذف ألفه وصلا وإثباتها وقفا. هذا ما لم يلقه همزة قطع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r4.claim: Worship God and no one else.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r4.anchor: {إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني} ولا تعبد غيري،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r5.claim: Mujahid explains the command as performing prayer in order to remember God within it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: أقم الصلاة لتذكرني فيها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r6.claim: Mujahid also says that one who misses a prayer should perform it when it comes to mind.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إذا تركت الصلاة ثم ذكرتها، فأقمها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r7.speaker: أنس عن النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r7.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that whoever forgets a prayer should pray it upon remembering; that is its only expiation. No grading is given.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r7.anchor: قتادة عن أنس قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها، لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك"

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r5.claim: The declaration is apposition to what is revealed and restricts it to affirming monotheism, the highest knowledge, alongside worship, the perfection of action.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r5.anchor: بدل مما يوحى دال على أنه مقصور على تقرير التوحيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r6.claim: Prayer is singled out and commanded because its purpose is remembering God, engaging heart and tongue in His remembrance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r6.anchor: خصها بالذكر وأفردها بالأمر للعلة التي أناط بها إقامتها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r7.claim: One interpretation takes the phrase to mean that God mentioned prayer in scripture and commanded it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r7.anchor: وقيل { لذكرى } لأني ذكرتها في الكتب وأمرت بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r8.claim: Another interpretation takes it to mean that God will remember Moses with praise.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r9.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r9.claim: A further interpretation means remembering God alone, without ostentation or mixing His remembrance with another's.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r9.anchor: أو { لذكرى } خاصة لا ترائي بها ولا تشوبها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r10.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r10.claim: Other interpretations take it as praying at times appointed for remembrance or as remembering one's prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r10.anchor: وقيل لأوقات ذكري وهي مواقيت الصلاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r11.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever sleeps through or forgets a prayer should perform it when remembering it, citing God's command to establish prayer for His remembrance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r11.anchor: لما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

DURR-FULL:v5p560/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the gate of Paradise bears God’s promise not to punish whoever says sincerely that there is no deity but Him.
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: مكتوب على باب الجنة: إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا لا أعذب من قالها

DURR-FULL:v5p560/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r4.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r4.claim: Anas recounts that ʿUmar converted after reading Ṭā Hā, including this declaration; Khabbāb then recalled the Prophet’s prayer for Islam to be strengthened through ʿUmar or ʿAmr ibn Hishām.
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r4.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: خرج عمر متقلدا بالسيف فاقيه رجل من بني زهرة فقال له: أين تغدو يا عمر

DURR-FULL:v5p560/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r5.claim: ʿAlī reports from the Prophet, Gabriel, and God that whoever comes with sincere testimony to God’s oneness enters God’s fortress and is safe from punishment.
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r5.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال: حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جبريل عليه السلام قال: قال الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r18.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r18.claim: One interpretation is “for my remembrance” in prayer; another is that God remembers Moses among the exalted through prayer, with the verbal noun construed actively or passively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r18.anchor: يحتمل أن يريد لتذكيري فيها أو يريد لأذكرك في عليين بها فالمصدر على هذا يحتمل الإضافة إلى الفاعل أو إلى المفعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r19.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r19.claim: Another group takes it to mean praying when one remembers God and His command, with the causal lām as in 17:78.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r19.anchor: وقالت فرقة معنى قوله لذكري أي عند ذكري إذا ذكرتني وأمري لك بها، فاللام على هذا بمنزلتها في قوله أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r20.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r20.claim: Three groups read للذكرى, لذكرى without the article, or للذكر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r20.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «للذكرى» ، وقرأت فرقة «لذكرى» بغير تعريف، وقرأت فرقة «للذكر»

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r4.claim: The first duty incumbent on those morally responsible is to know that none is worthy of worship but God alone, without partner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r4.anchor: {إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا} هذا أول واجب على المكلفين أن يعلموا أنه لا إله إلا الله،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r5.claim: To worship God is to affirm His oneness and perform worship for Him without associating a partner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r5.anchor: {فاعبدني} أي: وحدني وقم بعبادتي من غير شريك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r6.claim: One interpretation of the command is to pray in order to remember God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r6.anchor: {وأقم الصلاة لذكري} قيل: معناه: صل لتذكرني.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r7.claim: The preferred interpretation is to perform the prayer when one remembers God; Ibn Kathir says the hadith evidence supports this reading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه: وأقم الصلاة عند ذكرك لي. ويشهد لهذا الثاني ما قال الإمام أحمد:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r8.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r8.claim: The Prophet says that anyone who sleeps through a prayer or forgets it should pray when remembering it, citing this verse; Ahmad transmits the report, and the same ruling appears in both Sahih collections, with no other expiation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، عن أنس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا رقد أحدكم عن الصلاة، أو غفل عنها،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r18.claim: One explanation is that prayer is for remembering God, since His remembrance entails worship and praying to Him alone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r18.anchor: لتذكرني فإن ذكري أن أعبد ويصلي لي .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r19.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r19.claim: Mujahid says it means to remember God during prayer, which contains remembrances.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r19.anchor: أو لتذكرني فيها لاشتمال الصلاة على الأذكار عن مجاهد .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r20.claim: Other senses are because God mentioned prayer in scripture and commanded it, or so He may praise Moses and give him an honored reputation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r20.anchor: أو : لأني ذكرتها في الكتب وأمرت بها . أو لأن أذكرك بالمدح والثناء وأجعل لك لسان صدق .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r21.claim: It may mean remembering God alone with sincere devotion and seeking His face, without showing off or pursuing another end.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r21.anchor: أو لذكري خاصة لا تشوبه بذكر غيري أو لإخلاص ذكري وطلب وجهي لا ترائي بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r22.claim: Another sense is to remain mindful of God as the sincere are, keeping Him in mind; their trade does not distract them (24:37).
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r22.anchor: أو لتكون لي ذاكرا غير ناس فعل المخلصين في جعلهم ذكر ربهم على بال منهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r23.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r23.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r23.claim: It may refer to the appointed times of remembrance, namely prayer times, as in the command to remember God after prayer (4:103).
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r23.anchor: أو لأوقات ذكري وهي مواقيت الصلاة ، كقوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r24.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r24.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r24.claim: The lām can indicate a time, as in جئتك لوقت كذا and the wording of 89:24.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r24.anchor: واللام مثلها في قولك : جئتك لوقت كذا ، وكان ذلك لست ليال خلون . وقوله تعالى :

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r1.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r1.claim: The Prophet said that whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it should pray when remembering it; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r1.anchor: ( 684 ) ( من نام عن صلاة أو نسيها فليصلها إذا ذكرها )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r2.claim: The expected construction would be لذكرها, as in the hadith; explanations are that remembering prayer recalls God, that the omitted noun is my prayer, or that remembrance and forgetting are ultimately from God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r2.anchor: وكان حق العبارة أن يقال : لذكرها ، كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إذا ذكرها )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r3.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r3.claim: The Prophet also read the phrase as للذكرى.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p57/r3.anchor: وقرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( للذكرى )

MUQATIL:20:13-15/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r5.claim: Worship Me means affirm My oneness, since there is no god with Me.
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r5.anchor: فاعبدني } يعني فوحدني، فإنه ليس معي إله

MUQATIL:20:13-15/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r6.claim: Moses is to establish prayer in order to remember God.
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r6.anchor: وأقم الصلاة لذكري } [آية: 14] يقول: لتذكرني بها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r5.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r5.claim: One view is pray to remember God; another is pray so that God remembers and praises the worshipper in the highest company.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r5.anchor: فقيل: يحتمل أن يريد لتذكرني فيها، أو يريد لأذكرك بالمدح في عليين بها،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r6.claim: On the praise interpretation, the genitive may attach to the acting subject or the object of remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r6.anchor: فالمصدر على هذا يحتمل الإضافة إلى الفاعل وإلى المفعول

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r7.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r7.claim: Another explanation is maintain prayer after affirming God's oneness; prayer is itself remembrance and shows its rank as supplication before God.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r7.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أي حافظ بعد التوحيد على الصلاة. وهذا تنبيه على عظم قدر الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r8.claim: The Qurʾān calls prayer remembrance in the command to hasten to remembrance of God.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r9.claim: One who misses prayer through forgetfulness performs it when remembered; forgetfulness does not cancel the duty.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r9.anchor: وقيل: المراد إذا نسيت فتذكرت فصل كما في الخبر «فليصلها إذا ذكرها». أي لا تسقط الصلاة بالنسيان

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r4.claim: The sequence places knowledge of divine oneness before worship, then prayer, illustrating that foundational doctrine precedes practical branches.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r4.anchor: أنه سبحانه بعد أن أمره بالتوحيد ، أولا ثم بالعبادة ثانيا ، أمره بالصلاة ثالثا

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r5.claim: The fāʾ in فاعبدني makes worship follow from God’s divinity: God alone is entitled to worship.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r5.anchor: وأيضا الفاء في قوله : { فاعبدني } تدل على أن عبادته إنما لزمت لإلهيته

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r6.claim: Rāzī’s camp argues that the passage permits delaying clarification until the time of need: worship is commanded without its modality, and prayer without its form being specified.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r6.anchor: أمره بالعبادة ولم يذكر كيفية تلك العبادة فثبت أنه يجوز ورود المجمل منفكا عن البيان

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī replies that Moses may already have known the prayer God prescribed to Shuʿayb and earlier prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r7.anchor: لا يمتنع أن موسى عليه السلام قد عرف الصلاة التي تعبد الله تعالى بها شعيبا عليه السلام وغيره من الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r8.claim: Rāzī says prior knowledge of Shuʿayb’s prayer does not answer the command to worship; a new prayer would add benefit, whereas Moses could not doubt the known prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r8.anchor: حمل مثل هذا الخطاب العظيم على فائدة جديدة أولى من حمله على أمر معلوم لأن موسى عليه السلام ما كان يشك في وجوب الصلاة التي جاء بها شعيب

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī also allows that God explained the prayer at the time, though the Qurʾān does not recount that explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أنه تعالى بين له في الحال وأن كان المنقول في القرآن لم يذكر فيه إلا هذا القدر

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r10.claim: Rāzī replies that explicit explanation is more informative than an unelaborated command and thus would have been more fitting for the Qurʾān to narrate.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r10.anchor: لا نشك أن البيان أكثر فائدة من المجمل فلو كان مذكورا لكان أولى بالحكاية

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r1.claim: One gloss takes لذكري as remembering God, since His remembrance consists in worship and prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r1.anchor: لذكري يعني لتذكرني فإن ذكري أن أعبد ويصلي لي

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r2.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r2.claim: Mujāhid says prayer is for remembering God within it, since prayer contains remembrances.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r2.anchor: لتذكرني فيها لاشتمال الصلاة على الأذكار عن مجاهد

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r3.claim: Another gloss is that God mentioned prayer in the scriptures and commanded it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r3.anchor: لأني ذكرتها في الكتب وأمرت بها

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r4.claim: Another gloss is that God may remember Moses with praise and give him an honored reputation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r4.anchor: لأن أذكرك بالمدح والثناء واجعل لك لسان صدق

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r5.claim: Another gloss requires remembrance of God alone, unmixed with remembrance of anything else.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r5.anchor: لذكري خاصة لا تشوبه بذكر غيري

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r6.claim: Another gloss makes the purpose sincere remembrance and seeking God’s presence, without showing off or pursuing another aim.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r6.anchor: لإخلاص ذكري وطلب وجهي لا ترائي بها ولا تقصد بها غرضا آخر

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r7.claim: Another gloss is to remember God without forgetting, as sincere people keep Him in mind; the text links this to 24:37.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r7.anchor: لتكون لي ذاكرا غير ناس فعل المخلصين في جعلهم ذكر ربهم على بال منهم كما قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r8.claim: Another gloss takes the phrase as referring to the times of remembrance, meaning the appointed prayer times; it cites 4:103.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r8.anchor: لأوقات ذكرى وهي مواقيت الصلاة لقوله تعالى : { فإذا قضيتم الصلواة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا } ( النساء : 103 )

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r9.claim: A further gloss commands prayer when it is remembered, so an omitted prayer is made up upon recollection.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r9.anchor: أي أنك إذا نسيت صلاة فاقضها إذا ذكرتها

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r10.claim: Qatāda narrates from Anas that the Prophet said whoever forgets a prayer must pray it when he remembers, with no expiation other than that; Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r10.anchor: روى قتادة عن أنس رضي الله عنهما قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r11.speaker: الخطابي
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r11.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī’s first reading of the report is that nothing expiates a forgotten prayer except making it up.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r11.anchor: قال الخطابي يحتمل هذا الحديث وجهين . أحدهما : أنه لا يكفرها غير قضائها

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r12.speaker: الخطابي
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r12.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī’s second reading is that forgetting incurs no additional penalty or expiation, unlike intentionally missing Ramadan fasting or omitting a pilgrimage rite that requires compensation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r12.anchor: والآخر أنه لا يلزم في نسيانها غرامة ولا كفارة كما تلزم الكفارة في ترك صوم رمضان

RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r13.claim: Rāzī explains لذكرى as remembrance produced by God’s creation, or as an elision meaning لذكر صلاتي, remembrance of My prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18/r13.anchor: معناه للذكر الحاصل بخلقي أو بتقدير

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī recommends ordering missed prayers but holds that omitting the order remains valid; with ample time, make up the missed prayer first, while a tight current time requires the current prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r1.anchor: فلو ترك الترتيب في قضائها جاز عند الشافعي رحمه الله ولو دخل عليه وقت فريضة وتذكر فائتة نظر إن كان في الوقت سعة

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r2.claim: If a missed prayer is recalled after beginning the current one, al-Shāfiʿī says to finish the current prayer, then make up the missed one; repeating the current prayer is recommended, not required.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r2.anchor: ولو تذكر الفائتة بعدما شرع في صلاة الوقت أتمها ثم قضى الفائتة ويستحب أن يعيد صلاة الوقت بعدها ولا يجب

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa requires order among missed prayers until they exceed one day and night; recalling one during a current prayer invalidates it unless time is too short, after which both are made up in order.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله يجب الترتيب في قضاء الفوائت ما لم تزد على صلاة يوم وليلة

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r4.speaker: الحنفية
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r4.claim: The Ḥanafīs read لذكرى as when the prayer is remembered, taking the lām as ʿinda as in 17:78; they infer that missed prayers must be made up in order.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r4.anchor: حجة أبي حنيفة رحمه الله الآية والخبر والأثر والقياس ، أما الآية فقوله تعالى : { أقم الصلواة * لذكرى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r5.claim: The Prophet’s instruction that one who forgets a prayer should pray it when remembered is used by the Ḥanafīs as evidence for immediate make-up, since the fāʾ implies succession.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r5.anchor: أما الخبر فقوله عليه السلام : ( من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها ) والفاء للتعقيب

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r6.claim: Jābir reports that at the Battle of the Trench ʿUmar missed ʿAṣr until sunset was near; the Prophet had also not prayed it, then prayed ʿAṣr after sunset followed by Maghrib; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r6.anchor: وأيضا روى جابر بن عبد الله قال : ( جاء عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنهما إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الخندق

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r7.speaker: الحنفية
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r7.claim: The Ḥanafīs infer order from the Prophet’s consecutive prayers and from treating his action as clarification of the otherwise general command to establish prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r7.anchor: قالت الحنفية والاستدلال به من وجهين : أحدهما : أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( صلوا كما رأيتموني أصلي ) فلما صلى الفوائت على الولاء وجب علينا ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that one who remembers a missed prayer during congregational prayer should finish with the imam, make up the missed prayer, then repeat the prayer with the imam; the report may be attributed to the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r8.anchor: وأما الأثر فما روي عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أنه قال : ( من فاتته صلاة فلم يذكرها إلا في صلاة الإمام

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r9.speaker: الحنفية
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r9.claim: The Ḥanafīs use analogy: two obligatory prayers combined within one day and night, like the prayers at ʿArafa and Muzdalifa, retain their order, as should a small set of missed prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r9.anchor: صلاتان فريضتان جمعهما وقت واحد في اليوم والليلة فأشبهتا صلاتي عرفة والمزدلفة

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r10.speaker: أبو قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r10.claim: Abū Qatāda reports that when the group slept through Fajr and awoke after sunrise, the Prophet told them to move their mounts, then prayed the missed prayer; Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r10.anchor: حجة الشافعي رحمه الله أنه روى في حديث أبي قتادة : ( أنهم لما ناموا عن صلاة الفجر ثم انتبهوا

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r11.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r11.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī infers from the delayed Fajr make-up that recollection sets when the duty becomes binding without narrowing its time; current and missed obligations can therefore be performed in either order.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r11.anchor: فعلمنا أن ذلك الوقت وقت لتقرر الوجوب عليه لكن لا على سبيل التضييق بل على سبيل التوسع

RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r12.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that if order were a condition it would not lapse through forgetfulness, just as mistakenly praying Ẓuhr before noon at ʿArafa requires repeating both prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v22p18#2/r12.anchor: لأنه لو كان الترتيب في الفوائت شرطا لما سقط بالنسيان ألا ترى أنه إذا صلى الظهر والعصر بعرفة في يوم غيم
